proposals.summary: Dispatch r3/r1 buses from the terminal immediately when their route queue is large, instead of waiting for the headway target.
proposals.rationale: The strongest probe (dispatch at route_queue >= 3, -3.2%) shows the terminal headway hold is starving busy routes: r3 left 1,060 riders behind and r2 stranded 604 train transfers. Adding a high-priority dispatch-when-queue-large rule lets a bus leave as soon as there is real demand, cutting the worst left-behind queues at Old Main and Central while keeping the even-headway hold for quiet periods. No allocation change is made, so r2 keeps its 2 buses and Central transfers are not starved. Changes: Add bus_at_terminal rule: dispatch when route_queue >= 3 (priority 20, above even-headway); Keep 2/2/2 allocation, maxHoldS 60, and the even-headway terminal hold unchanged.

proposals.summary: Adopt the strongest probe: dispatch a bus from its terminal immediately when its route queue is already >= 3, so backed-up routes stop waiting for a headway slot.
proposals.rationale: The champion's only terminal rule holds buses at the terminal to even out headways, but the strongest measured probe shows that when a route already has a real queue (route_queue >= 3) dispatching immediately is 3.2% better. This directly attacks the top findings: huge queues left behind at Old Main for r3 (peak 229) and Central for r2 (peak 59), where holding a bus in layover only makes the backlog worse. The rule is guarded by route_queue so it never delays r2 at Central when it is empty and waiting for train transfers, and the even-headway rule still fires for low-queue cases. Changes: Add terminal rule: dispatch immediately when route_queue >= 3 (priority 20, above even-headway); Keep 2/2/2 allocation, even-headway hold, maxHoldS 60 and 45 s train dwell unchanged.

proposals.summary: Add the supported terminal fast-dispatch rule when a route queue is long, and let the Old Main r3/r1 stop skip the hold only when a crowd is already queued.
proposals.rationale: Probes show that dispatching a bus immediately at the terminal once its route queue reaches 3 is the strongest single change (-3.2%). Adopting it exactly keeps the change focused and within the evidence. No other rule or parameter is modified, so allocation stays 2/2/2 and minimum service is preserved. Changes: Added new bus_at_terminal rule probe-term-disp-routeque-3: dispatch immediately when route_queue >= 3.
